findings.mechanism: The asyncio.Queue is created without a maxsize, so it can grow without bound; a burst of events will accumulate indefinitely, exhausting memory and causing back‑pressure elsewhere.
findings.remediation: Change the queue initialization to asyncio.Queue(maxsize=1000) (or another appropriate limit) to bound the backlog.
findings.arithmetic: Queue is unbounded; offering 5000 events without draining will make _pending.qsize() equal 5000.

findings.mechanism: SQLAlchemy engine is configured with pool_size=10 and max_overflow=0, so only ten DB connections are available; 40 concurrent with_session calls will exceed this, causing connection blocking and worker saturation.
findings.remediation: Increase the pool size or allow overflow, e.g., create_async_engine(..., pool_size=20, max_overflow=10).
findings.arithmetic: With 40 concurrent sessions and a pool of 10, the number of active connections will reach the pool limit of 10 before additional calls block.

findings.mechanism: The function reads a Shipment, increments delivery_count in Python, and writes it back; concurrent executions can interleave, causing a lost update where the counter increments only once instead of twice.
findings.remediation: Perform the increment atomically in the database, e.g., use an UPDATE ... SET delivery_count = delivery_count + 1 with a WHERE clause or SELECT … FOR UPDATE before modifying.
findings.arithmetic: Two concurrent deliveries on the same shipment can both read the same initial count (n) and write n+1, resulting in a final count of n+1 instead of n+2; thus the final count can be at most 1 when starting from 0.

prediction.condition: 2 concurrent deliveries for the same shipment

findings.mechanism: The function queries all shipments then, for each shipment, performs a separate DB query to fetch the courier name, causing an N+1 query pattern that scales linearly with the number of shipments.
findings.remediation: Rewrite the query to join Shipment with Courier (or batch‑load couriers) so that courier names are retrieved in a single query.
findings.arithmetic: For 40 shipments, the code issues 1 query to fetch shipments plus 40 individual courier lookups, totaling 41 queries per request.
